messages:
anika: Quick readout from today's mid-cycle cutover. We triggered a rollback during canary at ~11:05 UTC due to increased memory growth on the v3.4 quant kernel. Impact: brief 3-minute latency spike on a single shard, no customer-facing errors.

devon: Thanks — can you share the immediate cause?

anika: Root cause appears to be a regression in KV cache eviction when the new kernel hits certain batch size patterns. Repro on staging w/ seq_length=2048 + batch=12.

ron: We observed the same on the dedicated pool. Canary config showed 18% error budget burn on one instance. Rolled back to kernel v3.3 and evictions returned to normal.

marie: SRE mitigations: 1) automatic fallback policy kicked in, 2) we scaled the canary pool down and limited burst capacity, 3) throttled incoming non-critical jobs.

leo: Deploy bot: deploy/rollout v3.4-quant-kernel -> rollback (id: d4f7c) completed at 11:08 UTC. Canary status: healthy after rollback. :white_check_mark:

anika: Action items: - engineering to open a small PR with a fix + unit test for eviction edge case (owner: devon) - add a canary threshold check for memory slope > 20%/min (owner: ron) - update runbook to include immediate canary scale-down steps (owner: marie).

devon: I'll push a fix by EOD and add a reproducer in the infra test harness. Patching quant kernel unit tests now.

marie: I'll update the runbook and add a new 'quiet window' note: no non-urgent schema changes during 1h before/after canary to avoid noisy trials.

ron: Also proposing a policy change: require two independent canary clusters (or AZs) for any kernel-level change that touches KV/cache. Low friction but extra check. Thoughts?

anika: +1 from me. Makes sense for stability. Let's make it a soft requirement for the next 30 days and revisit.

leo: Quick config snippet for the new canary memory check (example):
```
canary_policy:
  metric: memory_slope
  window: 60s
  threshold: 20%
  action: scale_down
```

anika: I'll schedule a brief postmortem doc and invite the oncall, runtime, and infra reviewers. Link will be posted in #postmortems in ~30m.

sre-bot: incident-1234 created (sev: low) — attaching logs and flamegraphs.

devon: heads-up: we found a poorly timed cache-clear in one test that made the issue reproducible. Fix will guard the eviction path.

marie: TL;DR for execs: brief rollback, no customer impact, root cause in eviction kernel, fix in progress, policy tweak to require 2-canary clusters for kernel-level changes. I'll draft a one-paragraph summary for the weekly exec update.

anika: Thanks everyone. Once devon posts the PR, let's run a staged canary with the new memory slope check and keep a tight watch for 2 hours. :eyes:

ron: Noted. Will update the canary dashboard with an alert for memory_slope > 12% too (for earlier detection).

leo: closing the loop: deploy/rollout d4f7c -> rollback verified. Leaving the canary hold for the patch. :thumbsup:
